You’re spot on with that interpretation. You kinda hit on this point too but Kevin is also showing the effects that fame can have on people. Like you said, he has been trying to relive his old childhood life for years now, searching for that simple, everyday, normal life. One without any expectations, without the responsibility that fame carries. Kevin is completely worn out of the famous life, and wishes he would have stuck with his heart as the younger version of himself. 

The year of 1999 is the most memorable time of his life, and also the most normal. By revisiting the house that formed his childhood memories, he is accepting the fact that this is the end of normality - he will never regain the old life he once had. Basically comes full circle for Kevin, and is certainly very very difficult for him to come to terms with. But it is something he felt was necessary to do.

Teach me empathy - this phrase that he is promoting is also essential. The livestream made this message surreal, as the “fans” of Kevin’s bombarded him for signatures of their materialistic possessions - which were then used for personal gain. Of course, there were real fans too, wanting to show nothing but empathy towards Kevin, as this entire situation was very hard for him to carry through with. The “fans” couldn’t care less about exploiting Kevin’s fame for their personal growth. He wanted empathy, he needed it to help him push through this immense challenge. 

Kevin is so smart, and definitely succeeded in making his message heard.
